question_text:
Show that a heat capacity of $3 R$ is a reasonable approximation to the specific heat of copper given in Table. Give your answer as the value of specific_heat.
(Reference to Table:
\begin{tabular}{lc}
\hline \multicolumn{2}{c}{ Values of Specific Heat for a Variety of Materials } \\
\hline Material & $\boldsymbol{c}_p[\mathbf{J} / \mathbf{k g} \cdot \mathbf{K}]$ \\
\hline Metals $^{\mathrm{a}}$ & \\
Aluminum & 900 \\
Copper & 385 \\
Gold & 129 \\
Iron $(\alpha)$ & 444 \\
Lead & 159 \\
Nickel & 444 \\
Silver & 237 \\
Titanium & 523 \\
Tungsten & 133 \\
Ceramics ${ }^{\text {a,b }}$ & \\
Al $\mathrm{O}_3$. & 160 \\
MgO & 457 \\
SiC & 344 \\
Carbon (diamond) & 519 \\
Carbon (graphite) & 711 \\
Polymers & \\
Nylon 66 & $1260-2090$ \\
Phenolic & $1460-1670$ \\
Polyethylene (high density) & $1920-2300$ \\
Polypropylene & 1880 \\
Polytetraflouroethylene (PTFE) & 1050 \\
\hline
\end{tabular}
)The unit of the answer is J/kg*K.
response:
## Result

$$c_p = \frac{3R}{M} = \frac{24.942}{0.06355} \approx 392.5\ \text{J/(kg·K)}$$

**Comparison:** The table value for copper is $385\ \text{J/(kg·K)}$. Our Dulong–Petit estimate of $\approx 392.5\ \text{J/(kg·K)}$ differs by only about 1.9%, confirming that $3R$ is indeed a reasonable approximation to the specific heat of copper.

$$\boxed{392.5}$$
